rationale: Both must win. Talarico leads Paxton by about 2-4 in October polls (Emerson +2, UH +2, TPOR +4, Marist +2); El-Sayed leads Rogers by about 2-4 in averages. Estimated P(TX) ~0.55, P(MI) ~0.68, positively correlated, so the joint is ~0.45. v4: the likeliest reason this is wrong is a Texas polling miss toward Republicans, as in 2018/2020/2024 (~45% chance a 2-3 pt lead evaporates), so trimmed to 0.43.

Base rate: Minnesota has not elected a Republican senator since 2002. Flanagan leads Tafoya by 3-5 in October polls (RCP +3.4, Mason-Dixon +4, SurveyUSA +3), but Cook moved the race to Lean D amid the welfare-fraud scandal. v4: the likeliest failure is late tightening plus a poll miss toward Tafoya (~20%), which the forecast already allows for, so it stays at 0.80.

The ECB hiked to 2.50% in September. Analysts (e.g. LBBW) see the next hike in December with new projections; core inflation of about 2.5% supports a hold in October. A search result showed OIS-implied hike odds, so I marked saw_market_price. v4: the likeliest failure is a hawkish surprise on the September 3.8% energy-driven headline inflation (~4%), so the forecast stays at 0.04.

The status quo is a fragile pause with no direct Israel-Iran strikes. But Netanyahu has pushed for renewed strikes, Trump reportedly refused only until after the Nov 3 midterms and signaled joint action soon, and CENTCOM plans are ready. The window runs through Nov 15. v4: the likeliest failure is a joint US-Israel strike in the Nov 4-15 window, with Iranian retaliation on Israel; I put that near 45%, so the forecast is a bit above a coin flip.

South Carolina is about R+15 and has not elected a Democratic senator since 1998. Polls show Graham ahead by about 2 (Trafalgar +3, Rasmussen +4; D-internal Impact Andrews +1), and Cook moved it to Lean R. Andrews holds a huge fundraising edge. One search result quoted a market price, so I marked it and ignored it. v4: the likeliest failure is a genuine Democratic-wave upset fueled by money and candidate weakness (~20%), so 0.80.

Acton leads Ramaswamy by about 3-4 in averages (Marist +7, BGSU +6, NYT/Siena +4; ActiVote outlier R+3), and Sabato moved the race to Lean D. But Ohio polls have overstated Democrats in recent cycles (Brown 2024, Ryan 2022). One search result quoted market odds, so I marked it and ignored it. v4: the likeliest failure is a repeat Ohio polling bias of ~4 pts (~40%), so I shaded from 0.62 to 0.58.

Democrats need a net gain of four. The environment favors them: Cook expects big House gains, Senate toss-ups include IA, KS, ME, MI, OH and TX, and non-market models give Democrats about 60-71%. Republicans keep control if they hold Texas or Ohio-type seats and a few toss-ups. v4: the likeliest failure is a systematic poll miss toward Republicans in red-state toss-ups (~40%), so R is set at 0.40.

Only a local Oleshky humanitarian truce and a failed energy ceasefire exist, and those categories are excluded. Russia says resumed talks imply no limits on combat, and the next round is mid-November in Abu Dhabi, after the deadline. Five days remain. v4: the likeliest failure is a surprise Trump-brokered general announcement (~2%).

Peltola leads Sullivan narrowly (DDHQ +2.4, RCP +0.8, DFP RCV simulation 51-49), and the lead has narrowed since August. Alaska leans R and incumbents usually survive, but Peltola won statewide in 2022. One search result quoted a market price, so I marked it and ignored it. v4: the likeliest failure is that Alaska polls understate Republicans and Trump's rally consolidates the base (~45%), so I put Sullivan at 0.42 rather than lower.

As of Oct 23-25, Anthropic's news page still shows Fable 5.1 as the latest. Leaks claim partners have access and a release 'next week', and an Azure listing appeared and was pulled; Opus, Sonnet and Haiku 5.5 have already shipped. Five days remain, and leak-based release timings often slip. v4: the likeliest failure is that the leaks are right and it ships this week (~35%), so I set 0.33.

YES means no US-Iran Hormuz agreement is announced by Nov 2. Talks are stalled; Iran ties reopening to seven conditions, the US adds enrichment demands, and shipping attacks peaked in October. Seven days remain. v4: the likeliest failure is a surprise pre-midterm deal announcement pushed by Trump (~5-6%), so 0.94.

Fighting is active (Houthi strikes on the Riyadh airport and near Mecca), and Riyadh publicly rejects a new ceasefire. However, the Saudi defense minister is in Tehran on Oct 26 with Pakistan and Turkey seeking de-escalation, and there is an unconfirmed $1B deal report. Both sides would need to announce a dated general ceasefire within five days. v4: the likeliest failure is a fast Tehran-brokered deal (~15%), which matches the forecast.
